newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Hanson and PM in angry war of words.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Hanson and PM in angry war of words.

text.p: Australia's race row politician, Pauline Hanson, on Saturday accused the Prime Minister of inciting thuggery, after another rowdy protest forced her supporters to cancel a political rally.

Hanson, whose attacks on Asian immigration and Aboriginal welfare have drawn strong support in opinion polls, blamed Prime Minister John Howard and the opposition Labor party for inciting an angry backlash against her new One Nation party.

"Last night, 200 of society's thugs intimidated and abused and attacked democracy," Hanson said in Hobart, capital of Tasmania state, where screaming protesters disrupted a meeting of her party on Friday night.
But Howard, who has resolved to confront Hanson after a year of playing down her political importance, said the independent legislator's accusation was stupid.
"That's plainly stupid and ridiculous and untrue," he thundered after speaking at the launch of an Australian-built warship at Williamstown docklands, near Melbourne.
"It's a desperately dishonest thing for her to say and I have for weeks been asking people not to demonstrate. I don't believe in violent demonstrations."

About 500 protesters threw eggs and shouted "shame" at One Nation supporters as they entered Friday night's meeting at Hobart City Hall. The meeting was called off before Hanson could speak after demonstrators tried to storm the stage.
Previous meetings of One Nation supporters have drawn angry protests around the country since Hanson launched her political party in her home state of Queensland last month.
Earlier on Saturday, Hanson, her voice wavering with emotion, described Friday's night protesters as "Howard's accomplices".

"Twenty-four hours after the prime minister and (Labor leader) Kim Beazley attacked me in the media, the civil disobedience they incited was perpetrated on honest, law-abiding citizens," she told a news conference.
"This is anarchy which we have not seen in Australia for decades," she added.

Howard, who was initially reluctant to respond to Hanson's remarks following her election to national parliament last year, went on the offensive last Thursday. He accused her of exploiting feelings of fear and instability in Australia.
Howard on Saturday urged people opposed to Hanson's views not to shout Hanson and her supporters down, saying this would play into her hands and boost One Nation's popularity.
"If you don't want Pauline Hanson's views to spread, don't demonstrate against her," Howard told reporters.
Hanson has called for a freeze on immigration, saying Australia risks being "swamped" by Asians, and wants the level of Aboriginal welfare scaled back.

Hanson's One Nation has recently outpolled Australia's third major party, the Australian Democrats. Support for Howard's government has fallen to its lowest level since it won office in March 1996, with most disaffected voters turning to Hanson.
